Content: Children live without fear.
Our level of governance has grown to the point where the way of being has changed. Children feel powerful by being part of the governing in big and small ways.
Children walking. Feet touching the ground, the water. Bellies breathing deeply.

Children are not shushed. The tree roots and tree tops are their teachers; the oceans offer lessons of patience and exhilaration; the sky is prayed to and for in thousands of languages and modalities; the buffalo truly roam;

While some kids covet roles - they are also content to laugh and play. They invent new roles in "outdoor school”. Their learning spaces are not separate from homes. Their communities of aunties and uncles and grandparents and brother/sister-cousins are their first teachers.
Young people would become masters of listening to the stories of other forms of life.

Getting around: It is not a pain in the ass to not drive. We get around on incredibly efficient public transit infrastructure. We think about transportation in ways that are local and global. Ridesharing is the norm. And we are consistently focused on non-fossil fuel. Travel is not the purview of only the middle and upper class. Travel for the sake of learning and connecting is valued and rewarded.
Children are healthy, happy, and safe. They are filled with songs and laughter, wonder and hope.
Youth are already poised to tell generational stories. Young people are already telling the stories of their ancestors.
Youth begin to find their purpose early.
Toddlers are laughing and playing outside with abandon, knowing people and animals all around are caring for these babies.
Kids are nourished for their inherent gifts and interests by all the people around them. Neighborhoods would see it as their responsibility. Different education for different needs.
Children and elders play together so they can find their purpose.

Cold, tasty water/sunny day and everyone has access to it; ancestor taking their own time waking up - hearing children laugh outside and adults laughing *big* - nobody is afraid to laugh big; doors are unlocked in case somebody needs something - hear someone coming in? oh, they need something; world that gets along due to safety, fear being gone; good fear exists (e.g. don't jump off a cliff, don't touch the stove); bad fear is erased; instead of talking about each other, we talk to each other; struggles have healthy confrontation and resolve; "I want to trust you with my children/grandma/etc."; people get to do what they love and what they're good at; good kind of teasing, good kind of support; freedom of not looking over your shoulder, chest out chin up; people being all the way who they are in these spaces; "...and it's good."

We play and learn with abandon. The kids play with abandon because their water is clean; their food is fresh. They remembered ancient stick games that teach them sharing and loving competition. When feelings arise like frustration or sadness, elders or caretakers are nearby to validate and acknowledge that tears are okay to flow. No one is mocked or fragile in the expression of emotions. In fact it is common to quietly rub a person's back when they need it (trying to not use the phrase "hold space").

Co-resistance and coregulation are practiced. We (re)member how to be connected, how to regulate. Children are now taught how to help themselves and other coregulate and reset. This is the first time when every living generation knows how to do this–so people being in a calm and regulated state is the norm.

There is a practice that is very popular with both kids and adults. Everybody makes noise and we try to harmonize with each other. Kids think it’s great fun. Adults recognize it teaches them how to play and be flexible in relationship with others.
Children grow and thrive into being with their own informed choices.
A child goes for a long walk and visits with other beings. The oldest tree, animals, and shrubs.
Our children are speaking to the trees and animals as they play outside, and they call out to us to let us know if any tending or care is needed.
Our children are nurtured, their wonder, awe and curiosity cultivated by all. Their uniqueness reflected back to them so they may thrive.
Childcare is mixed age and mixed generation where babies, toddlers, children are protected from generating lots of armor.
Babies feel loved, secure, have adventures in nature and love nature, learn to live in community. If we have healthy children that grow up, have a healthy future.

When kids get out into the grass they feel the memory and stories because they’ve been nurtured, have learned to feel the wisdom that comes from a place. Neighborhoods pay attention to each child so closely. Every member of a neighborhood contributes a square of a quilt for children on their 16th birthday that celebrates the gifts they bring to the community. Community connects children with the education that will help their gifts blossom … apprenticing etc. No concerns of homelessness, just focus on the gifts that we can bring, that can be fully cultivated in the community.

Children invite one another every day to places with amazingly fun names–like “Flight school”, “The Time Warp”, and “Peacemakers.” They are as popular as the movie theater or the beach. These places used to be known as spirit hubs, but since spirit hubs are essential to daily life, people just call them by the names they have picked up over years of community and shared practice. They radiate amazing energy, and smell like food and incense. You can hear laughter (all ages), chanting, and music from all corners of town.
Children learn to connect with their sacred gifts. Those gifts are seen as powerful.
Children’s councils that provide valuable input into community governance.
Children love to see and be around people that hold circles. There is such respect for people who help understand care better.

Every day the community’s children walk to the town square on streets without cars to start their day of learning and play. The sound of their playing and exploring rings through the air with the sound of birds and other wildlife. The children make food, create forts, and learn about the seasons. Every child in the community gets child centered, nature reverent, affirming education that celebrates the gifts that each of them brought to the planet.
Every child moves through their days feeling loved, cared for, and celebrated because they are here.
Children will gather by the bay and by the ocean for many of the specialized classes with elders and teachers. When the water needs something, it will be addressed quickly.
We have accepted the responsibility of being responsible for the well being of every child. The sink or swim culture is no longer supported. There is scaffolding and support.`I have lots of details.
Children go out to play and adults don't even care about them.
Original of Translation: Los niños salen a jugar y los adultos ni siquiera se preocupan por ellos.

Content: Children play with their own games, improvised.
Original of Translation: Los niños juegan con juegos hechos a mano, improvisados.

Content: We teach children skills that can be used for healing – gardening is healer, teacher and feeder.

Children are taught art, music, gardening, how to grow food, care for animals, openness, inclusivity – things that open their imagination, developing skills they can draw on as adults building community.
Our children will know no hunger.
Children share what they want to be when they are elders–because being an elder is coveted.

In the center of co-housing communities and eco-villages thrives community garden beds and the village childcare. Young children are cared for by village members and taught Indigenous ways of being. There is a core team of care providers and teachers who are supported generously by all of the adults of all ages in the village, from young adults to elders. Young children’s wellbeing is held as an utmost priority, reflected in centering their presence. The laughter, joy, cuteness, and wonder of the young children support the wellbeing of all villagers. Through multigenerational communities that cherish and care for your children, the generational fabric of the community is healed and maintained intact and flourishing. Children in the village spend their early years cultivating their heart, mind, body, spirits in deeply rooted connection to flora, fauna, fungi, and folks, forming foundational love and capacities that serve them and their villages seven generations back and seven generations forward.

Kids of every shade play in the field behind the church and its dancing barn.  Parents move in and out of small formations, making sure to catch up with each parent.  Parents are easeful about helping any of the children as needs arise … hair, food, clothing, hurt feelings, and curious enthusiasm.
Children learn about pleasure and consent in their early years, learning how to set and respect healthy boundaries with dignity.

Parents no longer feel the pressure to get their kids on a strict schedule and performance routine.  There is space, time, and resources for everyone to discover and move into their purpose.  Parents are able to move with the flow of what is needed for the day.

Young people have lots of outside learning. We focus on curiosity, care and storytelling as the roots of those multi age experiences. Dignity and learning and shared experiences drive those. Meaningful coming of age experiences - examples from indigenous communities. Every child, from the very first moment they are here are honored and known as bringing special things to the world.
That even the youngest can point to the plants and the ferns in the valleys and say their names in Hawaiian.

The descendants are born loved, and loving, and bright. They create a world of peace, joy, challenges, love, and healing. The descendants hold the wishes and dreams of the ancestors in their hearts and grow them. Life is not perfect, but it’s full and meaningful as every descendant holds the dream to be the ideal ancestor in their heart.
Children spend time with elders learning language and skills.
My babies can grow up fully able to see the stars.
Children play and are out in the streets without restriction.  We don’t need laws to tell them what to do and not do.

Children won’t want to have a job – they will want to take on roles with pride.  They will want to do the things they are good at.  They will be supported by the elders to learn the ways.  They will step into them with pride and support others in their roles.

Children remember their sense of awe and connection to nature and Spirit, in turn when they grow to adults they bring this ecstatic sense with them. Their perception and awareness of the world is one of wonder, awe and connection. Everyone treats each other with wonder and care.
Children are taught social skills, conflict resolution, and collectivisim from early age and these are deeply embedded in our culture.

Children opt into the types of math that fit their interest and curiosities in the world.  Children are no longer scared into careers because of the possibility of starving or not having a place to live – so they (with help from the community) find their passion and purpose and continue to evolve.
Children are told they can be anything they want to – children play music in the windows, teach the old game of football.  Grandpa walks the neighborhood streets to see if anything needs fixing.
Nourishing communities were built long ago for kids who have aged out of the foster care system.

We tell stories about the huge plot of land that was set aside for people who didn’t have families.  People have a hard time believing that not having an address etc. was a problem to living a life.  The huge plot of land was utilized in such a way that kids learned all kinds of stuff that they could contribute into the future.  It was a committed group of strong adults that made it happen, but the whole community started to listen with curiosity to what the youth knew was needed for the future.
Every child knows that they are a part of the good and hope that they want to see.

A young man is 18 years old. His name is Noah and has learned since childhood in classes offered in his compound how to listen to birds, value water, listen to nature. Noah wakes up listening to the birds that help him calm his own thoughts. His role in the compound in the Springtime is to work with barrels to collect rain water and bring the little ones home from school. 

He notices vines and moss and the beauty of Spring. He looks forward to creating mugs with his buddies that they will fire and use at the compound and some will be sold in the store outside the compound where people buy goods that are made by hand.

Children would be fully supported to find their first purpose and pursue it with all their might.  This means adults have built the capacity to be patient and curious about how a great variety of pursuits - some of which are seemingly so strange -  might be able to teach and nourish the community.  There is a story about the teen who became the tree sitter.  He simply sat with trees until he was in his 30’s.  It took a couple years for adults to realize that he shared a deep understanding of what each of the trees ecosystems where in need of at that moment.  It tested the resolve of the community to allow purpose to unfold…and to ensure everyone had the shelter, food, and care they needed to be healthy regardless of what they chose to do.

A universal understanding that we each have blood as well as spiritual ancestors/descendants as living beings of the Earth is established. In the light of this, vulnerable youth living with mental illness would be cared for in spiritual healing centres where they will be initiated into practices from the lineage of their spiritual ancestors, from their maternal as well as from their paternal side. They will be cared for within the safety of a sacred community for the individually-customized required length of time until the practices become an embodied habit like brushing teeth and then sent back to continue living with their families. This would support them to gradually lessen identification with the body and mind and align with their Spirit. In addition, these practices would support them like two wings, creating resilience and protection throughout their lives, and grant them the highest chance of realizing their purpose on Earth.
Children would learn by filling their own purposeful and valued roles within the community also according to capacity.

Children aspire to be the circle keepers and they know they don’t have to wait until adulthood to take on this role. They have learned this by watching groups of adults trying to navigate hard conversations over meals turn to a young person and ask if they would be interested in helping the conversation flow. The young person joyfully accepts the invitation and begins reminding the adults of the community norms for hard conversations and invites the adults to share with each other from their hearts, bodies, spirits and truths in deep respect for the hearts, spirits, bodies and truths their words will meet in this circle.
Children are taught from childhood to watch the chatter of their mind with compassion

Children are on the streets and parks playing without fear because people are caring for all the children, not just their children. The parents and loved ones of said children and in community with one another enjoying stories and are not worried about their children because they know their children are playing and safe. Said children are speaking in multiple languages with one another because there are no borders so languages seep freely in and out of communities and it is safe to learn from one another so children freely speak multiple languages even if they have not mastered fluency yet. The children take breaks by running to a nearby berry bush and Ancestor Izzy’s mango tree which now sits in Elder Emiliee’s great grand son’s yard. The trees bear fruit in abundance.

We want our kids to grow up without fear—without worrying about the future, or what global warming might mean for their own children. Without fear of deportations. We want children with stronger mental health, not exposed to so much violence, who feel safe in their homes and in their neighborhoods.

We hope they’ll have better opportunities—good jobs with fair wages—so they can afford a home of their own and live with more independence. We want better public transportation that is easy to use and affordable. Fewer illnesses. Access to health care and medicine at a price families can manage, so people don’t have to be afraid of seeing a doctor because it costs too much or means missing a day of work.
Original of Translation: Nuestros hijos no tienen miedo del futuro ni miedo de que les pasara a sus hijos por lo que está pasando con el calentamiento global. No miedo a las deportaciones. Niños con mejor salud mental no expuestos a tanta violencia, que se sientan seguros en sus casas y también fuera de sus casas. Mejores oportunidades de tener buenos trabajos con mejores salarios para que tengan la oportunidad de comprar una vivienda y ser más independientes. Mejorar el sistema de transporte que sea accesible y a bajo precio. Menos enfermedades. Acceso a los servicios médicos y medicamentos a bajo costo para que la gente no tenga miedo de ir al doctor porque perderá un día de trabajo y también el miedo al alto costo.

Content:
Wisdom flows primarily through our youngest and our oldest community members. They both guide the path forward while reminding us of our humanity. Our children are taught how to grow fruits and vegetables in elementary school, they plant community gardens that they can take home to their family. They learn how to respect animals, especially those that we eat. 
There is no more state testing in schools, no more iPads or digital whiteboards. Much of the learning is done via storytelling. Our children dream of being painters and architects and farmers and nurses, without having the pressure of what those salaries look like or how valued they would be considered in society.
My children understand and learn from their ancestors.
Kids can be kids, playing freely on the streets and parks
We know from our youngest years how to acknowledge harm and repair it.

Kids are taught songs and how to live in their bodies. It is a normal thing, kids would be raised to play instruments, sing together, and how to move in their bodies - no shame, moving together and playing together, it has all become normal.
Childhood is surrounded by a natural environment and access to food.
Every child can walk to a park and in the park people are planting, playing, restoring, enjoying, eating, singing, learning
Children are our joint responsibility, all cared-for, free & loved.
Children are protected by all.

When a child is born they begin training in human nature and reconciliation as early values toward becoming master reconcilers. When children are ready to accept the Master Reconciler role, they can move to provide their passion offering (what used to be called work). They move through collective decision-making/consensus. Repair, reconciliation, regeneration and love are the values.
All children grow up in communities that are wholly safe.
Our children witness a fierce commitment to care.
All the children play and roam with freedom, safety & joy.
Enough activities and resources for children and teenagers. That they can have inspiration for their future and receive scholarships.
Young people are taught the history of the people who came before them through storytelling. This is how they will look to the future.
Children’s artwork is all around the community, uplifting their imaginations
Children are raised intentionally to have body autonomy, say yes or no to things, grow food, flowers, pride parades and taking this experience allows them to flourish in many beautiful ways.

My granddaughter 6x removed awakes to the sound of rain or light. She is surrounded by relationships that nurture her.  She has a sense of purpose and embodies her values. She leans into abundance.  She has enough. She is joyful and makes room for fun. She strives to find the good in others, even in those she doesn’t really like. Likes trees and the sound of birds, and dirt on her feet.  Hugs, always hugs

Every child grows up knowing that they are sacred, and that they are loved as they grow.  They know how to process what happens and what is going on inside of them.  They learn how to do self healing, and preventative self care.  It’s hard to believe that used to be overlooked.  They learn resilience–and that they have community that supports them – and they can bring themselves back into regulation.
As children grow they learn the skills to become good parents. They get to practice as they are growing – built into their growing, exploring and learning.

All the children are ours, literally. We have reimagined what family is and we are all deeply responsible for all children in our city. They are swimming in and out of people’s houses and we trust the children.

Date/Circle Name: 10/30/25 Kailua, HI Kipuka Pala'a Group, Le Jardin Academy
Content: Young people share their voices advocating to step up. The young people planted the seed to be kind and cautious of their actions and influence others to do the good things now for this far off future.
Children grow up with awe & appreciation of those who come from another land or speak another language
Culturally we are more honest and open with our children about our history
Children are still learning, integrating experimentation, different social settings
Children are respected and seen as whole
Grown children don’t wonder about who their family was.
Children grow up and look back for inspiration and re-imagine the future.
Kids are playing, laughter everywhere, and get lots of rest.
Kids weave in and out of houses and yards and their laughter is a continual medicine.
On rainy days, the children spend time listening to how the raindrops land to receive instructions on what that will mean for the actions of the day.
A world of people, animals, and nature living in coherence where every child and living structure is celebrated and received with space and gratitude.
We will carefully record time and place of birth, date recorded with planetary activity, temperative, environment, the details will be respected as windows into knowing.
Children feel safe inside and outside of their homes
Children playing on the street, children fighting because they all want to win their games,
Resonated on the thought that it is possible to design and work towards a vision where a child can live, work, play, and stay.
Children are in a happy, unrestricted mood because they feel safe, secure, protected, and in a nonthreathening environment.

Children will have time and access for play, to learn how to swim and dance with the Elders. Elders will have the care and infrastructure they need to have a peaceful time aging, dancing, and feeling. Adults can work one job, one that they love and enjoy part-time so that the rest of the day we get to spend it cooking, visiting our families, dancing with friends and finding love.
Children socializing, dancing, singing and use their screens only for doing the same thing.
We teach our children how to care for and protect plants and animals.
Original of Translation: Le ensenamos a nuestros hijos como cuidar y proteger a las plantas y los animales.

Content: Only thriving communities where everyone can go far and be who they are. No more gangs. They are abolished. Only positive communities for our youth of  tomorrow.
Every child gets the proper  education.

The children who once ran through our homes became the adults who carried wisdom. They worked fewer hours, breathed deeper, laughed louder, and remembered that life was meant to be lived not only survived.
A world where every child has the opportunity to build their own future, making it better than their previous generation.
Technology is always changing allowing easy problem solving. We commit to help [every child] understand these skills and tools to use them in their favor.

Childcare is affordable and accessible for families. Children are prepared for each passing day in their lives, as well as a better future and our community. After jobs were lost, children were educated on how to survive in the future and how to survive without AI.
